Yohimbine Hydrochloride (BAN) Aphrodine Hydrochloride; Chlorhydrate de Québrachine; Co- rynine Hydrochloride; Yohimbina, hidrocloruro de; Yohimbine, chlorhydrate de; Yohimbini hydrochloridum. Methyl 17α-hy- droxy-yohimban-16α-carboxylate hydrochloride. C21H26N2O3,HCl = 390.9. CAS — 146-48-5 (yohimbine); 65-19-0 (yohimbine hydro- chloride). ATC — G04BE04. ATC Vet — QG04BE04. (yohimbine) Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii) and US. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Yohimbine Hydrochloride). A white or slightly yel- lowish, crystalline powder. Sparingly soluble in water; practical- ly insoluble in alcohol and in dichloromethane. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 3.5 to 5.5. Store in airtight containers. Protect from light. USP 31 (Yohimbine Hydrochloride). A white to yellow powder. Slightly soluble in water and in alcohol; soluble in boiling water. Store in airtight containers. Profile Yohimbine is the principal alkaloid of the bark of the yohimbe tree, Pausinystalia yohimbe (Corynanthe yohimbi) (Rubiaceae); it is also found in Rauwolfia serpentina. It is an alpha2-adreno- ceptor blocker with a short duration of action. It has an antidiu- retic effect and produces increases in heart rate and blood pres- sure.
